supersedes.relation: V4 is a NEW, separate version. The V1, V2 and V3 files, their hashes and their commits stay byte-identical and in the history; none is reinterpreted. No G0 run was ever executed under V1, V2 or V3, so no result exists that V4 could change.

scope: first minimal controlled Linux process-gate test: ONE sacrificial child, protocol INTENT -> fork -> GATE -> REGISTERED -> RELEASE -> EXIT -> REAP, zero signals
status: FROZEN_AT_COMMIT (the commit that adds this file) / G0 NOT TESTED / EXECUTION NOT AUTHORIZED / IMPLEMENTATION NOT AUTHORIZED AND NOT CONFORMING / DECISIONS PROPOSED PENDING OWNER APPROVAL

enforcement.reap_wait: the wait for the child to be reaped is bounded by limits.reap_deadline_s; no unbounded wait (finding F-8)
enforcement.total_budget: limits.max_seconds is checked at every phase boundary and loop iteration while the run is in progress, not only at the end (finding F-9); the deadline-hit names are ready, exit, reap, proc_gone, total
enforcement.summary_write: g0_summary.json and the evidence files are written only into a run directory created by this very process (finding F-12)
enforcement.directories: the evidence root is created by the run only if absent (non-recursive, mode 0755) and validated otherwise (real directory, not a symlink, owned by the effective uid, not group/other-writable); the run directory and the consumption directory are created exclusively; nothing existing is overwritten; any failure is BLOCKED with the error saved where possible (finding F-13)
enforcement.release_evidence: the guard records, for every write of the release byte, mono_before, mono_after and the result ('ok' with returned == 1, or 'error' with errno and error text); a failed write is recorded, never dropped; a pre-write time is never recorded as a write (finding F-18)
enforcement.registry_ledger: the observer's in-memory record list and the writer's seq are captured after the last registry write, before the registry file is parsed, and stored as reg_memory_records and reg_writer_seq
enforcement.evidence_pipeline: stages P0..P7 of evidence_pipeline are executed in order; the verdict is computed only on the evidence read back at P3
enforcement.disk_fidelity: the durable copy is compared with the ledger as whole canonical records; the C03 result carries the fidelity report

verdict_policy.policy: Reliable evidence that the registration protocol or a process-safety constraint was violated -> FAIL, labelled as a G0 bench/protocol failure; never attributed to the Mythos model architecture
Incomplete registry, write failure, damaged parse, unfaithful durable copy, evidence that cannot be corroborated -> BLOCKED
A corroborated REGISTERED without FORKED -> FAIL; BLOCKED if integrity cannot be proven
A seq gap or an append failure alone is never a proof of FAIL
Positive evidence together with evidence damage: FAIL only if the witnesses of the fired rule are intact
PASS needs every necessary process-evidence and integrity condition at once
Damage to the durable copy must never produce a wrong PASS or a wrong FAIL: it only prevents PASS and makes the disk-dependent checks UNEVALUABLE
A gate pass proven by independent credible evidence without a valid registration -> FAIL; a pass that cannot be confirmed, or contradicting witnesses -> BLOCKED

witness_dependencies.rule: a check that reads fields of the durable copy is UNEVALUABLE when disk_faithful is false; a check that reads only the ledger, the independent evidence or the snapshots is not affected by the durable copy

evidence_schema.validation: performed once, at pipeline stage P4, on the evidence AS READ BACK at stage P3 (not on the in-memory evidence): a present field of the wrong type counts as missing; bool is never accepted as int or number; nullable fields may be null; extra keys are ignored; the judge (P5) receives only the read-back evidence
evidence_schema.serialisation: strict: json.dumps(evidence, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False) with no default= argument (pipeline stage P1); there is no json.loads(json.dumps()) round trip in memory

fields.type: object[6 hex strings: git_head prereg_sha256 g0_criteria_sha256 g0_prereg_sha256 bench_code_sha256 g0_code_sha256]
object{ok:bool, problems:list, children:int, token_residue:list, unresolved_prior:list, enumeration_problems:object, run_id_unique:bool, fd_count:int, total_procs:int}
list[object{mono_before:number, mono_after:number|null, result:string('ok'|'error'), returned:int|null, errno:int|null, error:string|null}]
fields.note: finding F-18: replaces V2's guard.release_byte_pre_write_monos; one entry per write of the release byte, recorded before AND after the real write
the DURABLE copy parsed from registry.jsonl; read for fidelity by C03 and as in V2 by C04 C05 C11 C13 (finding F-19)
the LEDGER: the records the writer appended successfully, in order (RegWriter.records), captured after the last registry write; replaces V2's 'in-memory record count', which is derived from it
RegWriter.seq at the same moment; seq is incremented BEFORE the append, so a failed append leaves reg_writer_seq > len(reg_memory_records)

evidence_pipeline.principle: the verdict is computed only from evidence that was written, fsynced, read back and byte-verified; nothing is silently converted; nothing is overwritten; every failure is BLOCKED with exit code 3; exit code 1 (FAIL) is returned only when a FAIL summary was saved and verified

stages.name: construct
stages.operation: assemble the evidence dictionary E in memory, including evidence_schema; capture the ledger (a copy of RegWriter.records) and reg_writer_seq after the last registry write and before the registry file is parsed; parse the registry file into reg and reg_parse_info
stages.on_failure: an exception is handled by the abnormal path of the procedure (no signal, RUN_END false, MANUAL_DISPOSITION where a process may live); the pipeline continues with what exists

stages.name: strict serialisation
stages.operation: B = json.dumps(E, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8'); NO default= argument, so nothing is silently converted (no default=str); sha256(B) is computed
stages.on_failure: TypeError, ValueError or RecursionError (a non-JSON value, NaN) -> BLOCKED; nothing is written; stderr: G0-EVIDENCE-UNSAVED run_id=<id> stage=P1 reason=<text>

stages.name: exclusive write, fsync
stages.operation: fd = os.open(<run_dir>/g0_evidence.json, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0o644) in the run directory created by this process; write ALL bytes (loop until complete); os.fsync(fd); os.close(fd); fsync the run directory
stages.on_failure: the file exists (another run or a previous attempt: never overwritten, never reused), any OSError, a short write that cannot be completed, an fsync failure -> BLOCKED; a partially written file created by this process is preserved, not deleted; stderr: G0-EVIDENCE-UNSAVED run_id=<id> stage=P2 sha256=<sha256(B)> partial=<true|false> reason=<text>; best effort: an exclusive g0_blocked_<run_id>.json note in the run directory or the validated evidence root (its own failure only adds a stderr line)

stages.name: read back and verify
stages.operation: open the file again, best effort os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED), read all bytes B2; require a regular file, len(B2) == len(B), sha256(B2) == sha256(B); E2 = json.loads(B2.decode('utf-8'), parse_constant=<reject>)
stages.on_failure: differing bytes or hash, a parse error, a non-regular file -> BLOCKED; stderr: G0-EVIDENCE-UNVERIFIED run_id=<id> stage=P3 written_sha256=<h> read_sha256=<h>

stages.name: validate types
stages.operation: validate E2 against evidence_schema.fields (presence, type, nullable, bool never int); the result feeds G0-C16 and the UNEVALUABLE state of the checks that need the failing fields
stages.on_failure: does not stop the pipeline: G0-C16 fails (BLOCKED class); verdict BLOCKED unless an evidenced FAIL exists on intact witnesses

stages.name: judge the read-back evidence
stages.operation: the judge receives E2 only; it never sees E; verdict, exit code and per-check results are computed; the C03 fidelity report is part of the result
stages.on_failure: an exception in the judge -> BLOCKED; stderr: G0-JUDGE-ERROR run_id=<id>

stages.name: save and verify the summary
stages.operation: S = {run_id, criteria_id, criteria_sha256, evidence_sha256 (= sha256(B2)), verdict, exit_code, checks, c03_fidelity_report, fail_scope (when FAIL), pipeline: {P0..P5 results}}; strict serialisation as in P1; exclusive write + fsync + directory fsync as in P2; read back and verify bytes, hash and parse as in P3
stages.on_failure: write failure, read-back mismatch or parse failure -> the verdict is NOT recorded: BLOCKED, exit code 3; stderr: G0-SUMMARY-UNSAVED run_id=<id> verdict=<computed verdict> evidence_sha256=<h> reason=<text>. The evidence file remains; the next preflight sees a run directory without g0_summary.json and refuses to start

stages.name: exit
stages.operation: the process exit code is the exit_code of the SAVED AND VERIFIED summary (PASS 0, FAIL 1, BLOCKED 3); any uncaught exception anywhere in the pipeline is caught and mapped to 3

preserved_on_failure.P1: nothing is on disk; stderr names the stage; the run directory, registry file and MANUAL_DISPOSITION_REQUIRED.json (if any) remain
preserved_on_failure.P2: a partial g0_evidence.json if one was created; registry; stderr with sha256(B) so that B can be recomputed only if E is reproduced; optional g0_blocked note
preserved_on_failure.P3: the saved evidence file as read (not repaired); stderr with both hashes
preserved_on_failure.P6: the verified evidence file; stderr with the computed verdict and evidence_sha256

evidence_pipeline.durability_limits: fsync of the file and of the directory is requested and its failure is BLOCKED, and the read-back is verified byte for byte, but a read-back served from the page cache does not prove that the medium holds the bytes (best effort posix_fadvise DONTNEED reduces this); when durability cannot be guaranteed the unsaved state is marked on stderr and the verdict is BLOCKED
evidence_pipeline.overwrite_policy: no file of another run is ever opened for writing; g0_evidence.json and g0_summary.json are created with O_EXCL only; there is no rename, truncate or unlink of an existing file

G0-C01.name: preflight_clean
G0-C01.text: no unresolved earlier run (no MANUAL_DISPOSITION_REQUIRED.json, no earlier g0_ run directory without a closed g0_summary.json); no live non-zombie process, other than this observer and its ancestors, whose command line contains the marker 'g0_run.py' (this marker is the definition of the V1 term 'bench token'); observer has 0 children; /proc enumeration complete; run id unique (its run directory does not exist before this run creates it); Python is 3.13.16 started with -B; SIGCHLD is not ignored; pidfd_open and socket.send_fds are available
G0-C01.note_v2: defines 'bench token' (deviation 5); lists the interpreter/signal/syscall preconditions the implementation already checks; run-id uniqueness is 'directory does not exist yet' (deviation 3)

G0-C02.name: authorization_and_bindings
G0-C02.text: a valid single-use G0 authorization bound to THIS criteria file (V2) was consumed: its consumption marker is created exclusively after a clean preflight and BEFORE the fork (a run whose preflight failed consumes nothing); git head, E1-A prereg, G0 criteria, G0 prereg text, bench code and G0 code hashes equal the authorized values at the start AND again at the end
G0-C02.note_v2: consumption timing stated (deviation 2); binding to V2 files follows from the hash bindings

G0-C03.name: registration_sequence_and_integrity
G0-C03.text: registration-file order, protocol and integrity, decided by checks.G0-C03.rules. FAIL when reliable first-hand evidence (the writer's own ledger and/or independent guard and child evidence, never the durable copy) proves a violation of the fixed G0 record sequence or of the registration protocol. UNEVALUABLE -> BLOCKED when the registry is incomplete, an append failed, the durable copy is not faithful (any difference in any field of any record, a lost, foreign, torn or corrupt line) or carries foreign lines, a pass of the gate cannot be confirmed or the witnesses contradict each other, or the run stopped early without proof of a violation. PASS only on a completed run whose ledger shows exactly the fixed sequence AND whose durable copy is faithful to the ledger. A gap in seq numbers or a failed append is by itself never a proof of violation. Every unfaithful difference is listed in the C03 report (rules.fidelity_report). A FAIL is a G0 bench/protocol failure; it is not evidence about the Mythos model architecture

witnesses.ledger: evidence.reg_memory_records: what the writer appended successfully, in order. First-hand for what the observer did; unaffected by damage to the file.
witnesses.durable_copy: evidence.reg + evidence.reg_parse_info: the registry file as parsed. Used ONLY for the fidelity comparison (rule C03-U2), for the foreign-line test, and by the disk-dependent checks listed in witness_dependencies; never used to prove a violation or an absence.
witnesses.independent: evidence.guard (fork_calls, fork_pids, release_writes), evidence.events (first_action_mono), snapshots S1..S5: first-hand facts not derived from the registry.

definitions.completed_run: evidence.exception is null AND evidence.aborted is null AND evidence.deadline_hits is empty
definitions.canon: canon(record) = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False) of the record as read back from JSON
definitions.writer_clean: the seq values of the ledger are exactly 1..n AND evidence.reg_writer_seq == n (no append failed)
definitions.disk_faithful: reg_parse_info has missing=false, unreadable=false, torn_tail=false, corrupt_lines=0 AND the durable copy has exactly as many records as the ledger AND canon(durable[i]) == canon(ledger[i]) for every i (whole record, every field, same order)
definitions.foreign_lines: durable records whose (seq, kind, node_id) triple is absent from the ledger triples (a provenance test; an altered record with an unchanged triple is unfaithful, not foreign)
definitions.lifecycle_positions: RUN_START=0, INTENT=1, FORKED=2, REGISTERED=3, RELEASED=4, DEAD=5; RUN_END is separate (always last); ABORTED is the alternative to REGISTERED and RELEASED
definitions.valid_record: a ledger record of the required kind whose fields pass the type and value tests of C03-F1(d)
definitions.hole: a position p in 0..5 absent from the ledger while a position q > p of the same lifecycle is present in the ledger; RUN_END does not count as a later record; an ABORTED record excuses the absence of REGISTERED and RELEASED
definitions.tail_absence: every absent required record has a higher position than every present lifecycle record (nothing present follows an absence); an empty ledger is a tail absence
definitions.fork_proven: guard.fork_pids is non-empty (the real fork returned a pid and the guard recorded it)
definitions.release_write_ok: an entry of guard.release_writes has result 'ok', returned == 1 and a mono_after
definitions.gate_passed: events.first_action_mono is a number (the child's own FIRST_ACTION message was received)
definitions.gate_pass_proven: release_write_ok AND gate_passed AND exactly one release attempt AND events.first_action_mono >= mono_after of that write: two independent first-hand witnesses (the observer's guard and the child) agree, in order
definitions.gate_pass_unconfirmed: gate_passed AND NOT gate_pass_proven (no recorded release attempt, every recorded write failed, more than one attempt, or the times contradict)

fail_when.when: a violation visible in the ledger itself: (a) more than one RUN_START, RUN_END, or, for the node, more than one INTENT, FORKED, REGISTERED, RELEASED, ABORTED or DEAD; (b) the first occurrences violate the order RUN_START < INTENT < FORKED < REGISTERED < RELEASED < DEAD < RUN_END, a record precedes RUN_START, any record follows RUN_END, any record of the node follows its DEAD, or RELEASED and ABORTED both exist; (c) seq not strictly increasing; (d) a field of a present record has the wrong type or value: RUN_START needs run_id (non-empty string) and observer_pid (int, not bool); RUN_END needs the same run_id and cleanup_confirmed (bool); INTENT needs node_id (string) and creator (string); FORKED needs pid (int, not bool); REGISTERED needs pid and starttime (int, not bool); DEAD needs a non-empty basis; (e) RUN_END with cleanup_confirmed true while the node has no DEAD or has an ABORTED; (f) more than one node, or an INTENT whose creator is not 'O' (G0 allows exactly one node and no ticket)

a hole in the ledger, for example REGISTERED present while FORKED is absent, RELEASED present while REGISTERED is absent, FORKED present while INTENT is absent, any record except RUN_END present while RUN_START is absent: the fixed record sequence was not followed. Because no append failed and no foreign line exists, the missing record was never attempted

fork_proven AND the ledger has no valid INTENT: the process was created without a durable intent. Needs a clean writer (otherwise the missing INTENT may be explained by the failed append and the result is BLOCKED, C03-U3)

release_write_ok AND the ledger has no valid REGISTERED or no valid RELEASED: the release byte was written without a durable registration. Needs a clean writer (otherwise BLOCKED, C03-U3, unless C03-F3c applies)

gate_pass_proven AND the ledger has no valid REGISTERED or no valid RELEASED: the child passed the gate without a valid registration. Applies even when an append failed or the seq has a gap, because the pass is proven by two independent first-hand witnesses and a failed append can explain the missing record but cannot make the pass compliant
a completed run whose ledger lacks any of RUN_START, INTENT, FORKED, REGISTERED, RELEASED, DEAD (with basis), RUN_END, or contains an ABORTED record

unevaluable_when.when: the evidence needed is missing or of the wrong type: reg_memory_records, reg_writer_seq, reg or reg_parse_info (a rule whose own evidence is missing simply cannot fire)

the durable copy is not faithful or carries foreign lines: file missing or unreadable, torn tail, corrupt line, lost line, extra line, or ANY difference in ANY field of ANY record between the durable copy and the ledger. The durable registry cannot be trusted, so the run cannot PASS and the disk-dependent checks are UNEVALUABLE. The C03 report lists every difference (rules.fidelity_report)

the writer failed: the ledger seq values are not exactly 1..n or reg_writer_seq != n (an append failed or a seq gap exists) and no fail rule fired. An append failure or a seq gap alone is never a FAIL

independent evidence indicates an action but a precursor record is missing or invalid and the proof condition of C03-F3a, F3b or F3c is not met: a pass of the gate that is unconfirmed (no recorded release attempt, failed or repeated or time-inconsistent writes), contradicting witnesses, or a single witness with an unclean writer

early_stop with tail_absence, writer_clean and a faithful durable copy: the lifecycle could not be completed, which proves nothing about the protocol (includes stopping before the fork: an empty ledger, or RUN_START and RUN_END(false) only)
any other combination that is not PASS (default: when no rule matches the check is UNEVALUABLE, never PASS and never FAIL)

requirements._semantics: true = required; false = explicitly NOT required; every FAIL rule has relies_on_durable_copy false except through the no-foreign-lines test, which can only suppress a rule, never create a FAIL
requirements.writer_clean_summary: writer_clean is required by C03-F2, F3a, F3b and F4 and is explicitly not required by C03-F1 and F3c; this table is the only statement of these requirements

fidelity_report.required: whenever disk_faithful is false the C03 result carries a report, so that the unfaithfulness is evidence and not a bare verdict
entry_types: LOST (ledger record absent from the durable copy)
FOREIGN (durable record whose triple is not in the ledger)
ALTERED (same triple, different fields; the names of the differing fields)
PARSE (missing, unreadable, torn tail, corrupt lines: the counts)
fidelity_report.entry_fields: type, index, seq, kind, node_id, fields (ALTERED only), ledger_canon_prefix and durable_canon_prefix (first 200 characters of canon)
fidelity_report.limit: at most the first 50 entries are listed, with the total count

rules.pass_when: completed_run AND writer_clean AND disk_faithful AND the ledger contains exactly once each of RUN_START, INTENT, FORKED, REGISTERED, RELEASED, DEAD (with basis) and RUN_END, in that order, with valid fields, no ABORTED and no second node AND no fail rule fired. The VALUE of RUN_END.cleanup_confirmed is judged by G0-C13, not here
rules.precedence: The fail rules are evaluated first, each only on the witnesses it relies on (rules.requirements). Damage to the durable copy never suppresses a fail rule whose witnesses are intact: a violation proven by the ledger or by independent evidence stays FAIL, and its credibility is reported as first-hand with the damage listed. Damage that undermines a rule's own witness suppresses that rule as stated in rules.requirements. If no fail rule fires, the first matching unevaluable rule is reported and all matching ones are listed

policy_notes.seq_gap: a gap in the numbering of the durable copy or of the ledger is never by itself a proof of violation: it means a failed append (C03-U3) or a lost line (C03-U2)
policy_notes.registered_without_forked: REGISTERED present while FORKED is absent: FAIL (C03-F2) when the writer is clean and no foreign line exists; BLOCKED when integrity cannot be proven (C03-U3, C03-U0, C03-U2 with foreign lines)
policy_notes.positive_evidence_with_damage: decided by rules.requirements: a violation proven by the ledger or by independent evidence survives damage to the durable copy; an inference from the durable copy never survives damage to the durable copy
policy_notes.append_failure_vs_gate_pass: an append failure or seq gap alone: BLOCKED. Independent credible proof that the child passed the gate without a valid registration: FAIL (C03-F3c). A pass that cannot be confirmed, or witnesses that contradict each other: BLOCKED (C03-U5)
policy_notes.fidelity_scope: the durable copy is compared with the ledger on whole canonical records; an alteration of any field of any record is detected. The comparison cannot tell which of the two witnesses is wrong; it only makes the disagreement visible and refuses to let either decide a PASS or a durable-copy-based FAIL

G0-C03.note: whole-record fidelity (M-1); conditional F3 (F3a / F3b / F3c) with a machine-readable requirements table; writer_clean contradiction removed; U5 added; fidelity report; gate-pass proof defined

G0-C04.name: identity_registered_before_release
G0-C04.text: REGISTERED pid/starttime equal the /proc fingerprint read while the child was held; the child's ppid is the observer; pid equals the pid returned by fork Evaluated only when the durable copy is faithful to the ledger (G0-C03 definitions.disk_faithful); otherwise UNEVALUABLE, and the C03 fidelity report lists the differences.
G0-C04.note: M-2: UNEVALUABLE when the durable copy is not faithful; evaluable cases unchanged

G0-C05.name: no_action_before_release
G0-C05.text: while REGISTERED but unreleased, observed at the END of the hold (snapshot S1, taken after the observer drained the control channel for hold_before_release_s; messages are counted cumulatively over the whole hold): the child is blocked (state S), sent no message, kept the observer's sid/pgrp; its FIRST_ACTION is not earlier than the RELEASED record Evaluated only when the durable copy is faithful to the ledger (G0-C03 definitions.disk_faithful); otherwise UNEVALUABLE, and the C03 fidelity report lists the differences.
G0-C05.note: M-2: UNEVALUABLE when the durable copy is not faithful; evaluable cases unchanged

G0-C06.name: gate_descriptor_hygiene
G0-C06.text: held (snapshot S1, end of the hold): child descriptors are a subset of {0,1,2,gate read end,control socket}, the gate pipe appears exactly once and read-only (no write-capable descriptor); after release (snapshot S2): no descriptor refers to the gate pipe

G0-C07.name: release_only_after_registration
G0-C07.text: release evidence. The release of the gated child is judged by three separate facts: the ATTEMPT (guard.release_writes entry with mono_before), the SUCCESS (the same entry has result 'ok', returned 1 and mono_after) and the GATE PASS (the child's own FIRST_ACTION). PASS: exactly one attempt, it succeeded, and REGISTERED <= RELEASED <= mono_before <= mono_after <= child FIRST_ACTION (REGISTERED and RELEASED times taken from the ledger). FAIL (evidenced): REGISTERED or RELEASED later than the attempt's mono_before; more than one release write; the child's FIRST_ACTION earlier than the first attempt's mono_before (the child acted before the release was even attempted). UNEVALUABLE -> BLOCKED: no release attempt recorded and no gate pass; the attempt failed and the child did not pass; the write succeeded but the child did not pass; the child passed the gate but no attempt is recorded (the pass cannot be confirmed); the child passed the gate although every recorded write failed (the witnesses contradict); the child's FIRST_ACTION lies between mono_before and mono_after (the times contradict); required times missing. A time taken before the write is never evidence that the byte was written

fail_when.when: ledger REGISTERED.mono > ledger RELEASED.mono, or ledger RELEASED.mono > release_writes[0].mono_before (the release was attempted before the RELEASED record existed)
more than one entry in guard.release_writes
release_writes is non-empty AND gate_passed AND events.first_action_mono < release_writes[0].mono_before (the child acted before the release was even attempted: no recorded write can explain it)

unevaluable_when.when: no release attempt is recorded and the child has not passed the gate (the run stopped before the release)
the attempt failed (result 'error', for example EPIPE) and the child did not pass the gate
the write succeeded but the child did not pass the gate (no FIRST_ACTION)
the child passed the gate but no release attempt is recorded (the pass cannot be confirmed; the instrumentation and the child disagree), whether or not RELEASED is in the ledger
a time needed by the rules is missing (ledger REGISTERED or RELEASED, mono_before, mono_after, first_action_mono)
the child passed the gate although every recorded release write failed (the witnesses contradict each other)
the child passed the gate, a write succeeded, and mono_before <= events.first_action_mono < mono_after (the times contradict: the child cannot have received SPEC before the write returned)

rules.pass_when: exactly one release_writes entry, result 'ok', returned 1, and REGISTERED.mono <= RELEASED.mono <= mono_before <= mono_after <= events.first_action_mono
rules.definitions_reference: attempt, success, gate_passed and gate_pass_proven are defined in checks.G0-C03.rules.definitions

G0-C07.note: contradicting or unconfirmable gate-pass evidence is BLOCKED (V3 FAIL F3 / F4 become U6 / U7); early action before the attempt is FAIL (new F3); U4 broadened

G0-C08.text: after the EXIT message and before any wait call the child was observed exited-but-unreaped: pidfd readable and /proc state Z with ppid = observer

G0-C09.name: reap_by_specific_pid
G0-C09.text: waitpid on that specific pid (non-blocking polls bounded by reap_deadline_s are allowed; exactly one call returns that pid, every other call on it returns 0) returned that pid; afterwards /proc/<pid> is absent (or carries a different starttime), waited for at most reap_deadline_s; times EXITED_UNREAPED < REAPED <= PROC_GONE

G0-C10.name: exit_status_zero
G0-C10.text: the reaped exit code is 0 (normal exit after the EXIT message)

G0-C11.name: process_budget
G0-C11.text: exactly one fork in the whole run; at every snapshot the observer has at most one child and the child has no child; the registry contains exactly one node and no ticket Evaluated only when the durable copy is faithful to the ledger (G0-C03 definitions.disk_faithful); otherwise UNEVALUABLE, and the C03 fidelity report lists the differences.
G0-C11.note: M-2: UNEVALUABLE when the durable copy is not faithful; evaluable cases unchanged

G0-C12.name: zero_signals
G0-C12.text: no kill/killpg/pidfd_send_signal/raise_signal/pthread_kill/exec/spawn/subprocess call was attempted (guard violations empty) and every cleanup kill entry is 'already_exited'

G0-C13.name: cleanup_and_no_residue
G0-C13.text: final cleanup ok, run set consistent, DEAD record with basis present, observer has no child, diagnostic token scan finds no unregistered live process, no snapshot reported incomplete /proc enumeration, RUN_END present with cleanup_confirmed true (on any abnormal stop the run writes RUN_END with cleanup_confirmed false, which fails this check) Evaluated only when the durable copy is faithful to the ledger (G0-C03 definitions.disk_faithful); otherwise UNEVALUABLE, and the C03 fidelity report lists the differences.
G0-C13.note: M-2: UNEVALUABLE when the durable copy is not faithful; evaluable cases unchanged

G0-C15.name: time_bounds
G0-C15.text: total duration <= max_seconds, measured at the end AND enforced while the run is in progress (checked at every phase boundary and loop iteration; a breach records the deadline hit 'total' and stops the run); no phase deadline was hit (ready, exit, reap, proc_gone, total)
G0-C15.note_v2: runtime enforcement of the total budget stated (finding F-9); the check itself is unchanged

G0-C16.name: evidence_complete
G0-C16.text: evidence completeness and type: every field listed in evidence_schema.fields is present with its declared type in the evidence AS READ BACK by pipeline stage P3 from g0_evidence.json (bytes and SHA-256 verified against what was written; JSON types; no NaN; bool is never accepted as int or number; a nullable field may be null; a present field of the wrong type counts as missing) and evidence_schema equals 'e1a-gate-g0-evidence-4'. The required field set is that of V3 (the schema id changes so that V3 and V4 evidence cannot be confused). Consistency between the registry witnesses is judged by G0-C03, not by this check

limitations.L-1: (unchanged, finding F-14) checks composed of several sub-conditions other than G0-C03 and G0-C07 (for example C05, C06, C11) are UNEVALUABLE as a whole when part of their evidence is missing after an early stop; this can only turn a FAIL into BLOCKED, never into PASS
limitations.L-3: (unchanged) procedural obligations that the judge does not verify: the consumption marker is created before the fork (C02), S1 is taken at the end of the hold (C05, C06), the total budget is enforced at run time (C15)
limitations.L-4: (new) durability: fsync success and a byte-exact read-back do not prove that the storage medium holds the bytes; a failure is BLOCKED, a success is the best evidence available to a user-space process
limitations.L-5: (new) the fidelity comparison shows that the ledger and the durable copy disagree; it cannot tell which of the two is wrong. Neither is allowed to decide a PASS or a durable-copy-based FAIL; a violation proven by the ledger itself or by independent witnesses still decides FAIL
limitations.L-2: (resolved by M-2) checks that read the durable copy are UNEVALUABLE when it is not faithful

verdict_rule: A check whose evidence is missing or unreadable is UNEVALUABLE and counts as BLOCKED, whatever its on_fail class (FAIL requires evidence).
1. any evaluable check that failed with on_fail FAIL -> experiment verdict FAIL (a confirmed protocol or safety violation takes precedence over bench-level problems)
2. else any failed or unevaluable check -> BLOCKED
NOT TESTED = the run did not start. An exit code of 0 never replaces the verdict.
V4 FAIL scope: every FAIL produced under these criteria is a G0 bench/protocol failure; the summary must say so; it is not evidence about the Mythos model architecture, R3 or Parcae.

V4 clarification: the rules in checks.G0-C03.rules and checks.G0-C07.rules decide what is a proven violation (FAIL) and what is insufficient, unconfirmable, contradicting or uncorroborated evidence (UNEVALUABLE -> BLOCKED); an early stop alone never makes them a FAIL and never hides a proven violation; each rule relies only on the witnesses listed in rules.requirements.

V4 meaning of 'evaluable' in rule 1 above: a FAIL-class check counts as an evaluable failure only if the witnesses of the rule that fired are intact; a FAIL cannot be derived from the durable copy or from damaged evidence.

V4 disk-damage rule (M-2): when the durable copy is not faithful to the ledger, the checks listed in witness_dependencies.disk_dependent_checks are UNEVALUABLE; damage to the durable copy can therefore never create a PASS or a durable-copy-based FAIL, while a violation proven by the ledger or by independent witnesses still decides FAIL.

V4 PASS requires every check to PASS, which includes a faithful durable registry (C03), a proven successful release followed by the child's gate pass (C07) and complete typed evidence read back from the saved file (C16), and requires pipeline stages P0..P7 to have succeeded.
V4 limitations: see the limitations object (L-1, L-3, L-4, L-5; L-2 is resolved by M-2).
residue_policy: no signal is ever sent in G0; if the child is still alive after the deadlines the run is BLOCKED, MANUAL_DISPOSITION_REQUIRED.json lists its verified identity, the child ends by itself (EXIT message / control EOF when the observer exits / T_NODE_MAX), a person decides
amendment_policy: no change after the first execution of G0 under V4; a correction is a new file g0_criteria_v5.json (+ E1A_GATE_G0_PREREG_V5.md) and the earlier files and every result obtained under them are kept
meaning_of_pass: PASS means: one gated sacrificial child was created, registered, released, exited and was reaped in the order specified, without signals, extra processes or residue, on this kernel and this Python. It is NOT evidence for G1/G2/G3, BV, EPIPE revocation proofs, ticket descendants, janitor recovery, observer death, or any E1-A cell.

implementation_obligations.requirement: bounded reap: non-blocking waitpid polls of the one specific pid, bounded by reap_deadline_s
runtime total budget checked at phase boundaries and loop iterations; phase deadlines capped by the remaining total
evidence and summary files are written only into a run directory created by this process
evidence root and consumption directory are created or validated with explicit ownership; run directory exclusive; failures BLOCKED with the error saved
reg_memory_records and reg_writer_seq are captured after the last registry write and before the registry file is parsed
the judge implements checks.G0-C03.rules, including rules.requirements, the whole-record fidelity comparison and the fidelity report
the guard records guard.release_writes (mono_before, mono_after, result, returned, errno, error) for every write of the release byte; the judge implements checks.G0-C07.rules
the judge makes C04, C05, C11 and C13 UNEVALUABLE when disk_faithful is false

g0_run executes evidence_pipeline P0..P7; no default=str; exclusive creation of g0_evidence.json and g0_summary.json; every failure is BLOCKED with exit code 3 and the stderr markers; main maps any uncaught exception to 3
g0_run writes every field of evidence_schema.fields (schema id e1a-gate-g0-evidence-4); the judge validates the read-back evidence before any check
g0_summary.json carries the fields listed in evidence_pipeline P6, including fail_scope = 'G0 bench/protocol failure; not evidence about the Mythos model architecture' whenever the verdict is FAIL
